passage:
A community fridge stands outside the town center. Anyone can put food inside, and anyone who needs food can take it.
There are rules on the door. Food must be clean, fresh, and clearly marked with the date. Open drinks and half-eaten food are not allowed.
At first, some people worried that the fridge would become dirty or empty. But volunteers check it every morning and evening. Restaurants bring extra bread. Families leave fruit. Farmers sometimes bring vegetables that look strange but taste fine.
The fridge has become a quiet kind of help. No one has to explain why they need food. They simply open the door and take what they need.
